reports.remarks: We report the classification of AT2025izo as a Ia supernova based on an optical spectrum obtained with the Nordic Optical Telescope on 2025-05-04 (i.e., MJD 60800.11). The transient is coincident with the nucleus of the host galaxy. Comparison with a library of supernovae spectra using SNID (Blondin & Tonry 2007, ApJ, 666, 1024), suggests AT2025izo is an around peak SN Ia at a redshift of z~0.056. We note that there is significant MW extinction (Av=0.535) making the ~ current absolute magnitude at that redshift be Mg = -19.2 (with an intrinsic g-r colour of ~ -0.25).

reports.remarks: We report the classification of AT2023nnl as a Ia supernova based on an optical spectrum obtained with the Nordic Optical Telescope on 2023-07-25 (i.e., MJD 60150.01). Comparison with a library of supernovae spectra using SNID (Blondin & Tonry 2007, ApJ, 666, 1024) suggests AT2023nnl is an around-peak SN Ia at a redshift of z~0.06166. The redshift estimate is further confirmed by the identification of CaII H&K and NaID host galaxy lines.

This absolute magnitude and velocity is consistent with an SN Ia near maximum light.

reports.remarks: Using Superfit (Howell et al. 2005, ApJ, 634, 1190) and SNID (Blondin & Tonry 2007, ApJ, 666, 1024), we find best fits to SNe Ia near maximum light. The supernova is closest to SDSS J214857.26-090415.8. The best-fit redshift from snid is 0.083, which is what we adopt. Assuming this redshift we measure a Si II 6355 velocity of approximately 12,000 km/s. Adopting the distance modulus computed from this redshift (37.9), the r-band absolute magnitude of the object roughly coeval with the spectrum is -19.7 (apparent magnitude 18.3, from ZTF). This absolute magnitude and velocity is consistent with an SN Ia at maximum light.

Given the redshift of the host UGC 06719 (z = 0.021958, DM ~ 34.92; 2008MNRAS.383.1519C; values from NED), we measure a Si II velocity of approximately 14,000 km/s. The ZTF lightcurve displays a 1.6 mag increase in two days, up to a r-band magnitude approximately coeval with the spectrum of 18.3 (-16.6). The absolute magnitude and velocity corroborate the early phase. Further followup is encouraged.
